# kayjs-ui

> Components for kay apps. They ship as `.kay` sources that the app compiles as its own, and they are styled by the classes of one `theme.css`, which the app restyles from its own stylesheet. The set: buttons and icons, toasts, dialogs and a form dialog that calls a page's action, a sortable table, switches, checkboxes and chips, tabs and segmented controls, inputs, selects and pickers, cards, badges, notices, avatars, popovers and tooltips, page layouts and panels, a command palette, a tree view, charts, drag and drop, a markdown editor, media galleries, a cropper, pagination, QR codes, and a carousel, a star rating and a site menu for marketing pages.

## Rules that are easy to get wrong

- Import each component by its `.kay` path: `import Button from '@kaynooo/kayjs-ui/button.kay'`. Types, `toast`, `attempt`, `editing`, `infiniteList` and the defaults come from the package itself: `import { toast } from '@kaynooo/kayjs-ui'`, and the drag and drop controllers from `@kaynooo/kayjs-ui/dnd`.
- Components write no Tailwind utility, only the classes of `theme.css`, every one prefixed `kui-` as its tokens are, so a site's own `btn`, `card` or `--color-accent` never meets them. A rule of the app's on one of those classes restyles every instance; utilities passed through a component's `class` prop restyle one.
- Any parent, a layout and a page included, passes an island children and slots without parameters, which the server renders as static markup. A component or a page without a `--- server` fence passing one a function, a block with parameters or a class instance (such as Tabs' `@panel`, a Table's `@cell` or a function `rowKey`) renders as an island itself; a layout, or a page with a `--- server` fence, cannot, and moves that markup into a component of its own.
- `toast` only shows in the browser, called from an island. The server's copy of the toast list is shared by every request, so it stays empty. Render one `Toaster` and one `TooltipHost` in the root layout. A kay extension may render its own as well: while one is mounted, a second renders nothing, and takes over once the first unmounts.
- An icon is either a slot name such as `'close'`, which the app's settings map to any icon set, or an icon imported from `~icons/<prefix>/<name>`. The default slots use Tabler, so the app installs `@iconify-json/tabler`.
- Dialog and FormDialog follow `open`. The parent sets it, then sets it back to false in `onClose`, which runs however the dialog closed. Their content renders only while they are open. A Popover the page opens through `open` is set back the same way, in `onToggle`.
- FormDialog calls the action with the form's `FormData`. The server reads it as a plain form post, so give each control the `name` of its field in the action's schema: numbers, booleans and lists are coerced from their text, and files and the honeypot come along.
- Messages about the app's data are its own, passed as props (`failure`, `message`, `label`). The library holds English words for its own controls only:
  - Each is replaced through the prop of that name: `loadingLabel` (`Loading…`), `closeLabel` (`Close`), `backLabel` (`Back`), `resizeLabel` (`Resize list`), `empty` (`No data yet.`, MediaGallery's `No media.`), `copiedLabel` (`Copied!`), CopyButton's `failure` (`Could not copy to the clipboard`), MarkdownEditor's `uploadFailure` (`Could not upload the image`), Rating's `label` (`N out of M`), Carousel's `label` (`Carousel`), `previousLabel` and `nextLabel` (Carousel's `Previous slide` and `Next slide`, MediaGallery's `Previous` and `Next`), Carousel's `slideLabel` (`Slide {n} of {count}`) and `dotLabel` (`Go to slide {n}`), MediaGallery's `openLabel` (`Open full size`) and `itemLabel` (`Media {n}`), ZoomPane's `zoomInLabel`, `zoomOutLabel` and `fitLabel` (`Zoom in`, `Zoom out`, `Fit`), ImageCropper's `cropLabel` and `cropText` (`{w} by {h} pixels at {x}, {y}`), SiteNav's `menuLabel` (`Menu`), ConfirmDelete's `label` (`Delete`), `title` (`Confirm Deletion`), `confirmLabel` (`Delete`), `pendingLabel` (`Deleting…`) and `cancelLabel` (`Cancel`), FormDialog's `savingLabel` (`Saving…`) and `cancelLabel` (`Cancel`), SaveForm's `dirtyLabel` (`Unsaved changes.`), `cleanLabel` (`No unsaved change.`), `savingLabel` (`Saving…`), `saveLabel` (`Save`) and `discardLabel` (`Discard`), RangeInput's `fromLabel` and `toLabel` (`{label} from`, `{label} to`), MultiSelect's `allLabel` (`All`), `noneLabel` (`None`), `emptyLabel` (`No match`) and `selectedLabel(count)` (`{n} selected`), IconPicker's `searchLabel` (`Search icons`), `placeholder` (`Search icons…`), `gridLabel` (`Icons`), `searchingLabel` (`Searching…`), `emptyLabel` (`No icons found.`), `clearLabel` (`Clear icon selection`) and `moreLabel` (`Show more`), Carousel's `pauseLabel` and `playLabel` (`Pause`, `Play`), Toaster's `dismissLabel` (`Dismiss notification`), MarkdownEditor's `keysHint` (`Tab indents a list item; Escape then Tab leaves the field.`), ContributionGraph's `label` (`Contributions`), Table's `countLabel(count)` (`{n} rows`), `placeholder` (MultiSelect's `Any`, CommandPalette's `Search`, MarkdownEditor's `Write markdown…`), MultiSelect's `searchLabel` (`Search`), and CommandPalette's `label` (`Search`), `emptyLabel` (`No results`), `resultsLabel(count)` (`{n} results`), `siteSearchLabel` (`In the pages`) and `siteSearchError` (`The pages could not be searched`).

## Setup

kayjs-ui is published as `@kaynooo/kayjs-ui` to `https://git.kaynooo.fr/api/packages/kaynooo/npm/`, beside kay. kay, Tailwind v4 and `@iconify-json/tabler` are peer dependencies. It is released with kay at its version and peers on kay's minor: the app installs the one matching its kay and moves them together.

```sh
bun add @kaynooo/kayjs-ui @iconify-json/tabler
```

`src/app.css`, imported by the root `_layout.kay`, imports the theme right after Tailwind. kay collects the classes of the library's templates along with the app's own, so no `@source` line has to point into `node_modules`:

```css
@import 'tailwindcss';
@import '@kaynooo/kayjs-ui/theme.css';
@source '../.kay/classes.txt';

@theme {
  --color-kui-accent: light-dark(#3b6fd4, #7aa2f7);
}
```

The theme's tokens are `@theme default`, so the app's `@theme` overrides any of them wherever it sits. Each colour is `--color-kui-<name>`, used as `bg-kui-<name>` and the like, and holds `light-dark(light, dark)`:

- Surfaces, deepest first: `mantle`, `canvas`, `surface0`, `surface1`.
- Hairlines: `surface2` and `overlay0`.
- Text: `text`, `overlay1` (the faintest), `subtext0` and `muted`.
- State: `accent`, `accent-hi` (its hover), `on-accent` (text on it), `success`, `warning`, `info` and `error`.
- Fills: `fill-hover`, `fill-danger` and `row-hover`.
- Fields: `field-border`, the solid border of a text field, which buttons, Toggle tracks, carousel dots and empty Rating stars draw too, at 3:1 on every surface, so an app changing its surfaces sets it to match; and `field-focus`, the border of a focused text field, `accent` unless set.
- Stamps (`Badge(stamp)`): `stamp` (its ink and hairline), `stamp-fill` and `stamp-fill-hover` (its ground while a `.group` holding it is hovered).
- Chart series: `chart-1` to `chart-6`.

A few components take tokens for their box and type, for a skin restyling them without redeclaring their selector:

- Badge: `--kui-border-badge`, `--spacing-kui-badge-x`, `--spacing-kui-badge-y`, `--text-kui-badge`, `--tracking-kui-badge`, `--kui-badge-case` (`none` or `uppercase`) and `--kui-badge-font`, the text's own unless set, such as to `var(--font-mono)`; `--kui-border-stamp` for a stamp.
- Text fields, `kui-field-input` and a FormField's controls: `--spacing-kui-field-x` and `--spacing-kui-field-y` for the inset, `--kui-field-focus-shadow` for a shadow while focused, `none` by default, such as `3px 3px 0 var(--color-kui-accent)`.
- Notice: `--kui-border-notice` and `--font-weight-kui-notice`, which a compact one takes too.
- Avatar: `--kui-border-avatar` and the colour `--color-kui-avatar-ring` for its ring, `--font-weight-kui-avatar` for the initial. The two borders follow `--kui-border-card` unless set.
- Offset shadows and a press-down, `none` and `0px` by default: `--kui-shadow-raised` under a Card, CardRow, Widget and toast, `--kui-shadow-press` under a Button and a framed IconButton (solid or danger), which move down by `--kui-press-travel` and drop that shadow while pressed. A brutalist skin: `--kui-shadow-raised: 4px 4px 0 var(--color-kui-text)`, `--kui-shadow-press: 3px 3px 0 var(--color-kui-text)`, `--kui-press-travel: 3px`.

The theme is dark unless the visitor's system asks for light. `data-theme="light"` or `data-theme="dark"` on `html` wins over both, for a site with its own switch, and on any element it themes what that element holds. A colour the app overrides with a single value stays that value in both.

```kay
---
import Toaster from '@kaynooo/kayjs-ui/toaster.kay'
import TooltipHost from '@kaynooo/kayjs-ui/tooltip-host.kay'
import '../app.css'
---
slot
Toaster
TooltipHost
```

## Settings

The icons the components draw come from slots, each named for what it means: `alert`, `back`, `chevron`, `close`, `delete`, `globe`, `info`, `menu`, `pause`, `play`, `plus`, `search`, `spinner`, `star`, `success`, `zoomFit`, `zoomIn`, `zoomOut`. The app replaces any of them through kay's library settings, spreading the defaults:

```ts
// kay.config.ts
export default defineConfig({ settings: { '@kaynooo/kayjs-ui': './src/ui-settings.ts' } })
```

```ts
// src/ui-settings.ts
import type { Settings } from '@kaynooo/kayjs-ui'
import { defaults } from '@kaynooo/kayjs-ui'
import close from '~icons/lucide/x'

const settings: Settings = { ...defaults, icons: { ...defaults.icons, close } }

export default settings
```

`kay check` checks this module against `Settings`. The server, the browser, `kay build` and `kay test` all render with it.

## Components

Each component spreads the other attributes it is given onto its root element, `id`, `aria-*` and `data-*` included. The exceptions: Toggle and Checkbox spread them on their checkbox, Popover on its panel, and CommandPalette, ConfirmDelete, FormField, FormDialog, SaveForm, Menu, Toaster, TooltipHost, LoadMore and WhenVisible take none.

### Icon, Button, IconButton

- `Icon(icon="close")`: an `svg.kui-icon`. It is decorative unless `label` names it for screen readers. `icon` is a slot or an imported `~icons` icon.
- `Button(label="Save" variant="accent" icon="plus")`:
  - `variant` is `default`, `accent` or `danger`.
  - Its label stays on one line; a row of buttons wraps whole buttons, as the dialog and panel footers do.
  - A promise returned by `onClick` holds that button alone busy (spinner in place of the icon, `aria-busy`) and disabled until it settles; a rejection is logged. A `type="submit"` button is busy (spinner, `aria-busy`, clicks ignored) the same way, but not disabled, while its `onClick` or its form's `onSubmit` returns a promise.
  - An explicit `busy` shows a spinner and sets `aria-busy` and has the last word; it does not disable the button.
  - `expanded` sets `aria-expanded`, for a button that opens a panel.
  - `type` defaults to `button`, so a button inside a form never submits it by accident: pass `type="submit"` to submit. Children render after `label`.
  - `href` makes it a link looking like a button, `a.kui-btn`, taking a link's attributes such as `target` in place of `type`, `expanded` and `disabled`. A site path in `href` is not checked against the pages the way a literal `a(href)` is.
- `IconButton(icon="delete" label="Delete")`: an icon alone. `label` names it for screen readers and shows as its tooltip through TooltipHost. `size` is `xs`, `sm`, `md` or `lg`; `variant` is `solid`, `ghost`, `inline` or `danger`.

### toast and Toaster

```ts
import { attempt, toast } from '@kaynooo/kayjs-ui'

toast.success('Saved')
toast.error('Could not save')
toast.info('Copied')

// Resolves to what the call returned (`true` for a call returning nothing), or to undefined once it threw and `failure` was toasted, or a refusal of the whole call such as a limit.
const post = await attempt(() => publish({ id }), 'Could not publish')

// `success` is toasted once the call goes through.
if (await attempt(() => archive({ id }), { failure: 'Could not archive', success: 'Archived' }))
  selected.set([])

// A refusal of the action's handler, `ctx.fail(409, { error: 'Already published' })`, toasted as it says.
await attempt(() => publish({ id }), 'Could not publish', (data: { error: string }) => data.error)
```

`attempt(run, failure, refused?)`, or `attempt(run, { failure, success?, refused? })`, toasts, for a call that throws, the message `refused` reads from the data the action's handler passed to `ctx.fail`; else a refusal of the whole call, such as a limit; else `failure`. An empty or undefined answer from `refused` falls through to the next. Type `refused`'s parameter as the handler's data: `(data: { error: string }) => data.error`.

A toast stays for six seconds, an error for ten, or until its close button is pressed, named by `dismissLabel` on Toaster. Screen readers hear each one from a status region kept in the page, an error from an alert region. Its clock stops while the pointer rests on the toasts or focus is inside them, and goes on with the time it had left once both are gone. Toaster is a manual popover in the top layer, so toasts show above an open dialog.

### Dialog, ConfirmDelete

```kay
Dialog(open={editing()} title="Rename" onClose={() => editing.set(false)})
  @footer
    Button(label="Cancel" onClick={() => editing.set(false)})
    Button(label="Rename" variant="accent" onClick={rename})
  input.kui-field-input(name="name")
```

- Dialog is a modal `dialog`. It closes when its parent sets `open` to false, on Escape, or on a click outside. `onClose(event)` runs however it closed. Closed by Escape or a click outside, its content is still there to read; closed by the parent, it is already gone. Its title names it for screen readers, an `h2` unless `level` says otherwise.
- Once something has been typed inside, or while `dirty` is set (for example while a request is in flight), Escape and a click outside leave it open: only its own buttons close it.
- `ConfirmDelete(message="Delete this post?" failure="Could not delete" onConfirm={remove})` renders a trigger that opens a dialog asking before deleting:
  - While the promise `onConfirm` returns is pending, the dialog's buttons are disabled.
  - Once it resolves, the dialog closes. If it throws, the dialog stays open and `failure` is toasted, or a refusal of the whole call such as a limit, as `attempt` does.
  - `refused` reads a refusal of the action's handler, as `attempt` does, and its message is toasted in place of `failure`: `ConfirmDelete(... failure="Could not delete" refused={(data: { error: string }) => data.error})`.
  - `trigger="button"` makes the trigger a labelled danger button rather than an icon, and `trigger="link"` a plain underlined text button, for a confirm inside running text. `label` renames the trigger, for "Revoke link" or "Empty trash", and `class` goes on it. `size` and `variant` style the icon trigger only, `size` also sizing the cancel button when asking inline.
  - `success` is toasted once `onConfirm` went through, as `attempt`'s is.
  - `title` (`Confirm Deletion`), `confirmLabel` (`Delete`) and `pendingLabel` (`Deleting…`) replace the dialog's words: `ConfirmDelete(message="Rotating breaks every link already shared." failure="Could not rotate" onConfirm={rotate} trigger="link" label="Rotate link" title="Rotate link" confirmLabel="Rotate" pendingLabel="Rotating…")`.
  - `tone="neutral"` is for a confirm that is not a deletion, such as a save with a consequence: accent buttons, a check icon, and the title and confirm button worded by `label` (`Confirm`) unless given: `ConfirmDelete(tone="neutral" trigger="button" label="Save" message="Save without your own IP?" failure="Could not save" success="Saved" onConfirm={save})`.
  - `ask="inline"` asks in place instead of in a dialog, for a row of a list: a click hides the trigger and shows a danger button saying `confirmLabel` and a cancel button, the focus on the first. `message` names the pair for screen readers and is the danger button's tooltip. Escape or cancel brings the trigger back, focused; a failed delete toasts and stays armed, the focus back on the danger button.

### Table

```ts
import type { Column } from '@kaynooo/kayjs-ui'

const columns: Column<Post>[] = [
  { key: 'title', header: 'Title', sortValue: true },
  { key: 'views', header: 'Views', numeric: true },
  { key: 'author', header: 'Author', cell: false },
]
```

```kay
Table(columns={columns} rows={posts} rowKey="id" filter={['title', 'author']} filterParam="q")
  @cell(post, column)
    if column.key === 'title'
      a(href={`/posts/${post.id}`}) {post.title}
    else
      | {post.views.toLocaleString()}
  @empty
    EmptyState(title="No posts yet")
  @noMatch
    EmptyState(title="No post matches")
```

- With a `@cell(row, column)` block, every column shows what it draws, but one with `cell: false`, which shows the row's value at `key` as text, as every column does without the block. A table where any column sets `cell: true` draws only those through the block.
- `numeric: true` marks a count or an amount: aligned to the end, its digits in columns, sorted by its own value and largest first, each overridable by `align`, `sortValue` and `defaultDirection`.
- A column with `sortValue` sorts when its header is clicked. `true` sorts by the row's value at `key`; a function sorts by what it returns.
- The first click sorts in `defaultDirection`, `desc` unless set, and the next click flips it. `sort` gives the sort to start from.
- `serverSort` leaves the rows in the order they came. The headers show the sort, and `onSort(sort)` lets the page fetch the rows sorted that way, from a load or an action.
- With `sortValue: true`, dates sort by time, booleans as 0 and 1, and a missing value sorts last in either direction.
- `rowKey` is a field of the row or a function of it, and tells rows apart across a sort.
- `filter` shows a search box above the rows, `filterLabel` (`Filter`) naming it, and keeps the rows where a value it reads holds the typed text, case and surrounding spaces ignored: the fields it names, or what a function of the row returns, `filter={post => [post.title, post.author.name]}`. `filterParam="q"` keeps the text in the page's URL as `?q=`, which the server reads too, so a reload or a shared link renders filtered. Screen readers hear how many rows the typed text keeps from a status region, worded by `countLabel(count)`. `@noMatch` shows when the filter hides every row, `@empty` when there are none.
- Narrower than 30rem, its own width and not the screen's, so a table in a sidebar does it too, each row stacks as a card: a line per cell, its column `header` beside it as the label, the labels as wide as the longest up to 40% of the card, every value starting right after its label whatever its column's `align`, which a wide table keeps, and only the sortable headers kept, as a row of sort buttons. A column with an empty `header` spans the card's width. `narrow="scroll"` keeps the table whole and scrolls it sideways instead. A stacking table's wrapper is a size container, so it takes its width from its parent and never from its content: in an `auto`-sized grid column it collapses, where `narrow="scroll"` does not.
- `selectable` puts a checkbox on each row and, above the rows, a select-all box (ticked, indeterminate or not) with `N selected` beside it, a status screen readers hear, once rows are picked, outside the table so stacked cards have it too. `selected={keys}` gives the keys to start from (a new list from the parent is followed) and `onSelect(keys)` hears every change, the keys in the rows' order. A key whose row is no longer in `rows` leaves the selection, `onSelect` told, so a reload or an infinite list's new rows never keep a ghost; select-all acts on the rows the filter shows and leaves hidden ones as they are. `@bulk(keys, clear)` draws the page's bulk actions beside the count while something is picked, `clear()` emptying the selection: `Table(columns={columns} rows={sites} rowKey="name" selectable)` then `@bulk(names, clear)` holding `Button(label="Disable" onClick={async () => { await disable(names); clear() }})`. Row boxes are named `Select <first column's text>`; `selectAllLabel` (`Select all`, also the column's header for screen readers), `selectedLabel(count)` (`{n} selected`) and `selectRowLabel(row)` replace the words.

### Segmented, ChipGroup, TabNav, SiteNav, Tabs, Toggle, Checkbox

```kay
Tabs(tabs={[{ value: 'details', label: 'Details' }, { value: 'reviews', label: 'Reviews' }]} value="details" label="Product")
  @panel(tab)
    if tab === 'details'
      ProductDetails(product={product})
    else
      Reviews(product={product})
```

- `Segmented(options={[{ value: 'day', label: 'Day' }, { value: 'week', label: 'Week' }]} value="day" label="Period" name="period" onChange={period.set})`: real radios, so arrow keys move between options and the group posts as `name` inside a form. A parent passing another `value` moves the choice, and `null` picks none, for a state matching no option, such as a zoomed range beside a period picker. Without `name`, the group draws one unique on the page, which keeps two groups apart.
  - `onChange` may return a promise, as Toggle's may: the group is `aria-busy` and takes no other pick until it settles, and goes back to the previous option when it resolves to `false`, rejects or throws (logged), unless the parent set `value` meanwhile.
- `TabNav(links={[{ href: '/settings', label: 'Profile' }, { href: '/settings/keys', label: 'Keys' }]} current={ctx.url.pathname} label="Settings")`: tabs as links, one page each. The current tab is marked `aria-current="page"`, and a bar too narrow for every tab scrolls to centre it, without moving the page. `current={ctx.url}` with `keep={['period', 'site']}` carries those params of the page's URL onto each link that does not set them itself, for tabs sharing filters; a URL `current` marks the link whose path matches and whose own params the URL holds.
- `SiteNav(links={[{ href: '/', label: 'Home' }, { href: '/rooms', label: 'Rooms' }]} current={ctx.url.pathname} label="Main" menuLabel="Menu")`: a site's main links, in a row from the `lg` breakpoint and folded behind a menu toggle below it, which closes on Escape, a followed link or a press outside.
  - The page on screen is marked `aria-current="page"`, and a link to a section holding it `aria-current="true"`, as `/rooms` for `/rooms/blue`; `/` only marks itself.
  - The menu closes as a link is followed, on Escape, which hands the focus back to the toggle, and once `current` changes, as for a `persist` island kept from page to page.
  - It takes data alone, so a static layout holds it, with the logo and any call to action beside it in the app's own header.
- `Tabs`: panels that switch in place, without navigating, for settings or a product's details; use TabNav when each tab is a page of its own.
  - A `tablist` of buttons, each paired with its `tabpanel` through ids drawn with `uid()`. `@panel(tab)` draws each tab's panel once, hidden while another tab shows, so what a panel holds survives a switch.
  - A click, or the arrows (wrapping), Home and End, show a tab and focus it; only the shown tab is in the page's tab order. `onChange(value)` runs on each switch, and a parent passing another `value` shows that tab.
  - A panel not shown is `hidden="until-found"`, so the browser's find in page or a link to an id inside it shows its tab, and so does kay's `focusInvalid`: after a refused save, `focusInvalid(form)` shows the tab holding the first field marked `aria-invalid` and focuses it, with no work out of which tab that is.
  - It renders inside an island, since its panels come from a block.
- `Toggle(label="Public" checked={post.public} name="public" onChange={setPublic})`: a checkbox drawn as a switch, with `role="switch"`, that posts like a checkbox. Without `label`, give it `aria-label`.
  - `onChange` may return a promise: the switch is `aria-busy` and flips no further until it settles, and goes back where it was when it resolves to `false`, rejects or throws (logged), unless the parent set `checked` meanwhile. A void answer leaves the switch as clicked. The switch jumping back is all the user sees, so toast the failure too. `attempt` resolves to `undefined` on failure, so turn that into `false`: `onChange={async checked => (await attempt(() => setPublic({ id, public: checked }), 'Could not publish')) ?? false}`.
- `Checkbox(label="I agree" checked={agreed()} name="terms" onChange={agreed.set})`: a native checkbox and its label, posting like one. `hint` adds a quieter note after the label, and `indeterminate` draws it as neither ticked nor not, for a box over a partly ticked list: a click toggles it from `checked`, and it is drawn so again while the parent keeps `indeterminate`. Without `label`, give it `aria-label`. `onChange` may return a promise, as Toggle's may. Use Toggle for a setting that applies as it is flipped.
- `ChipGroup(options={[{ value: 'films', label: 'Films' }, { value: 'games', label: 'Games', icon: 'star' }]} value={decks()} label="Decks" name="decks" onChange={decks.set})`: chips to pick several options from, real checkboxes posting each picked option under `name` (one unique on the page without it). `onChange` gets every picked option in the order of `options`, and may return a promise, as Segmented's may. An option may be `disabled`. A parent passing another `value` moves the picks.

### Pagination, QrCode

- `Pagination(page={page} pages={pages} url={ctx.url})`: links to the pages of a list through the URL's query, so it renders on the server with no island and each page has a URL of its own.
  - Each link keeps `url`'s path and query, `param`, `page` by default, set to its page and left out for the first one. Read the page in a server fence: `const page = Number(ctx.url.searchParams.get('page') ?? 1)`. A page past the ends, or no whole number, such as `?page=abc`, shows as the nearest that exists, so clamp it the same way where the page's own query reads it.
  - It shows the first and last pages and `siblings` on each side of the current one, 1 by default, an ellipsis for those left out, or the page itself when only one would be. The current page is marked `aria-current="page"`; Previous and Next are links with `rel="prev"` and `rel="next"`, and plain text at the ends. With one page or none it draws nothing.
  - `label` (`Pagination`), `previousLabel` and `nextLabel` replace its words.
- A list whose length is unknown, which fetches one row past the page to know whether another follows, passes `more` in place of `pages`, and gets Previous and Next alone, Next a link while `more` is true: `Pagination(page={page} more={next !== null} url={ctx.url})`, or by offset, `Pagination(offset={offset} limit={20} more={next !== null} url={ctx.url})`, which steps `?offset=` by `limit`, `param` then being `offset` by default. With no step to link, it draws nothing.
- `Pagination(of={list})`: the same links for a page kay's `paginate()` from `kay/content` gave, `const list = await blog.page(ctx.params.page) ?? ctx.notFound()` in a `blog/[[page=integer]].kay` route, each page at its own path, `/blog`, `/blog/2`, rather than through the query. `of` takes any `{ page, pages, href(n) }`.
- `QrCode(value={shareUrl} label="Scan to open the list" size={160})`: the value as a QR code, an SVG image drawn where the page renders, on the server for a static page. `label` is its `alt`, and may be left out for a decorative code, which is then hidden from assistive technology. Without `size` it takes the width CSS gives it.
  - `inline` draws the SVG in the page instead of an image, so the colours in `options` may be CSS ones and follow the page: `QrCode(value={url} inline options={{ foreground: 'currentColor', eyeColor: 'var(--color-accent)', background: null }})`. A `label` then makes it `role="img"`; `size` sets the box's width and height.
  - It keeps dark modules on a light ground with a quiet zone, which every scanner reads, whatever the theme. `options` takes what `qrCodeSvg` from @kaynooo/utils does, `ecc`, `moduleShape`, `eyeColor`, `foreground`, `background`, `margin` and the rest, its colours written out since the image cannot read the page's CSS, unless it is `inline`.

### TextInput, Textarea, Select

- `TextInput(value={title()} onInput={title.set} onChange={save})`:
  - `onInput(value)` runs on each keystroke, and `onChange(value)` once the value is committed, on blur or Enter. `onBlur(event)` gets the box's own blur, as on an `input`.
  - `type="number"` hands back a number, or `null` once emptied, to both callbacks, and takes a number, `null` or a string as `value`: `TextInput(type="number" value={count()} onInput={count.set})` with `signal<number | null>(1)`. A box partway through a number, such as `1,`, reports nothing until it parses. A parent writing back its own spelling of the same number leaves the caret alone.
  - Without `value` and `onInput` it is a plain field keeping what is typed, for a form posting to an action without JavaScript: `TextInput(name="email" type="email" required autocomplete="email")`, with `value` to start it filled. kay refills only the fields a form's own template writes, so pass `value={failure?.values.email}` to keep what a refused post sent.
- `Textarea(value={notes()} onInput={notes.set})`: the multi-line TextInput, taking the same props, `rows` among the rest, and working as a plain field without `value` and `onInput`. While focused it keeps the text as typed, and takes the parent's reading of it, such as without a blank line, once left.
- `Select(value={kind()} options={[{ value: 'post', label: 'Post' }]} onChange={kind.set} emptyOption="Any")`:
  - `value` and `onChange` take the type of the options' values, so a union stays a union and a number option hands back a number: `const kind = signal<'post' | 'page'>('post')` passes `kind.set` with no cast.
  - `emptyOption` adds a first option worth `''`, labelled by the string, or blank with `true`; `value` and `onChange` then take `''` too, so hold a `signal<Kind | ''>`.
  - `loading` shows a disabled row saying `loadingLabel` while the options are on their way.
  - The right option stays chosen when the options arrive after the value.
  - `submit` submits the form holding it once an option is picked, after `onChange`, for a GET filter form (see Forms).

### Card, Badge, EmptyState, Notice, Avatar

- `Card(title="Traffic")`: a `section.kui-card` that frames its children in `.kui-card-body`. `head` sits at the far end of the title's line, for a count or a link. `bare` drops the body's inset, for content that runs to the edge, such as a table. The title is an `h3`, or the heading `level` given, from 2 to 6.
- `Badge(label="Draft" tone="warning" icon="info")`: `tone` is `neutral`, `accent`, `success`, `warning`, `danger` or `info`. Children render after `label`. `stamp` draws it as a rubber stamp: a hairline in its ink, small spaced mono capitals, its ground turning `stamp-fill-hover` while a `.group` holding it, such as a card link, is hovered. A tone colours a stamp as it does a badge.
- `EmptyState(title="No posts yet" description="Write the first one.")`: what a list shows when it holds nothing. `level` (1 to 6) makes the title a heading, `level={1}` for one standing for the whole page, such as a 404, which then needs no hidden `h1`; without it, the title is a paragraph. An `@actions` block sits below the description, for the button that adds the first item: `EmptyState(title="No posts yet")` then `@actions` holding `Button(href="/new" label="New post")`.
- `Notice(tone="error" label={failure})`: a form's outcome or a refusal, in place. `tone` is `info`, `success`, `warning` or `error`; an error is `role="alert"`, read out at once, the others `role="status"`. Children render after `label`, for a link to follow up. It is a bordered box, for a page section; `compact` drops the box, for a line under a form.
- `Avatar(src={user.avatar} name={user.name} size="sm")`: the picture, or the name's first letter on a colour seeded by the name when `src` is empty or fails to load; a new `src` is tried again. `size` is `xs`, `sm`, `md` (the default) or `lg`. It is decorative, the name being written beside it, unless `label` names it for screen readers.

### Popover, TooltipHost

```kay
Popover(placement="bottom-end")
  @trigger(attributes)
    IconButton({...attributes} icon="chevron" label="More")
  Button(label="Duplicate" onClick={duplicate})
```

- Popover is the browser's popover, which needs Chrome and Edge 114, Firefox 125 or Safari 17, and it sits beside its trigger through CSS anchor positioning, Chrome and Edge 129, Firefox 147 or Safari 26, so an older browser opens it away from the trigger. A click on the trigger toggles it, and a click outside or Escape closes it. The panel draws an id unique on the page, pairing it with its trigger; an `id` given instead must be unique too, and made of letters, digits, `-` and `_`, since it also names the CSS anchor.
- `@trigger(attributes)` renders the trigger, which spreads `attributes`: `popovertarget`, `aria-expanded` and its anchor.
- `placement` is `bottom-start`, `bottom-end`, `top-start` or `top-end`, and the browser flips it when there is no room.
- `open` opens or closes it from the page, and `onToggle(open)` runs however it changed: a page driving `open` sets its own value back there, or it could not open the panel again after a click outside closed it.
- TooltipHost shows the `data-tooltip` of whichever element the pointer or a tab lands on. `data-tooltip-placement`, a CSS `position-area`, says where it sits, `top` by default: `button(data-tooltip="Copy link" data-tooltip-placement="bottom")`. IconButton sets `data-tooltip` to its label. The pointer can cross onto the tooltip without it closing, and Escape closes it until the pointer or the focus moves to another element.

### PageHeader, PageSection, CollapsibleSection, Widget, CardRow, SidePanel, SplitLayout

```kay
PageSection(title="Moons")
  @actions
    a(href="/moons/new") New moon
  CollapsibleSection(title="Archived" open={false} boxed)
    @meta
      Badge(label={archived.length})
    for moon of archived
      CardRow
        @left
          Icon(icon="success")
        @right
          span {moon.radius} km
        @actions
          a(href={`/moons/${moon.id}`}) Edit
        | {moon.name}
```

- `PageHeader(title)`: the head of a page, its one `h1`. `@meta` sits beside the title, for a badge, a count or a link back, `@actions` after it, past a divider, `description` is a quieter line under the title's, and the children come under that.
- `PageSection(title)`: a titled `section` of a page, its `h2` one level under the page's own, or the heading `level` given, `1` for a section holding a whole page. `@actions` sits at the end of the head line.
- `CollapsibleSection(title)`: a native `details`, so it folds without script and a static page can hold it. `open` is whether it starts unfolded, `true` by default. `boxed` draws it as a card whose title is a band over a padded body. `@meta` sits in the band before the chevron, for a count the folded section would hide.
- `Widget(title icon)`: a dashboard tile, a framed body under a head line of icon, title and `@actions`. `isEmpty` swaps the body for the `@empty` block, keeping the frame; with no `@empty` block, an empty widget renders nothing.
- `CardRow`: one line of a list drawn as cards. Children are its body, `@left` leads, `@right` trails, and `@actions` comes last, dimmed until the row is hovered or focused.
- `SidePanel(open title onClose)`: a modal `dialog` along the edge, driven by `open` like Dialog and named by its title. `@actions` sits in its head before the close button, such as previous and next; `@footer` under its body. A click outside, Escape and its close button all close it through `onClose`; `closeLabel` names that button, `Close` by default.
- `SplitLayout`: a list and a detail pane side by side from `md` up, given as `@list` and `@detail`, each with an optional `@listHead` and `@detailHead`.
  - `@sidebar` adds a navigation column left of the list, rendered once: below `md` it is an overlay shown while `sidebarOpen` is set, titled `sidebarTitle`, whose back button calls `onSidebarClose` for the parent to set it back to false.
  - Below `md`, `detailOpen` shows the detail pane in the list's place.
  - `resizableList` adds a handle on the list's right edge, a `separator` dragged with the pointer or moved 20px at a time with the arrow keys, between 180px and 560px. `listWidthKey` keeps the width in `localStorage` under that key: the page renders at 260px, then takes the kept width once mounted.
  - It renders inside an island, since its panes are blocks and its handle has handlers.

### Stat, Meter, BarList, SiteFavicon, CopyButton, Rating

- `Stat(value={12} label="moons" icon="info")`: a figure read with what it counts.
- `Meter(value={usage} label="Disk" fillClass="bg-kui-warning")`: a `role="meter"` bar holding `value` between 0 and 100. `fillClass` styles the fill alone, such as a colour picked by threshold.
- `BarList(rows={[{ key: 'fr', label: 'France', value: 120, display: '120 visits' }]})`: a bar per row, each measured against the largest value, reading `display` or else the value. `onSelect(row)` makes each row a button, from an island; `empty` is what it reads with no rows. Its rows are typed `BarListRow`, or any type extending it.
- `SiteFavicon(src={site.favicon} name={site.name})`: a site's icon, or the `globe` slot in a colour drawn from `name` when `src` is missing or fails to load.
- `CopyButton(text={url} label="Copy link")`: copies `text`, with `html` alongside for apps that paste rich text, and reads `copiedLabel` for two seconds. It takes Button's `variant`. A copy the browser refuses toasts `failure`.
- `Rating(value={4.6} max={5} label="Rated 4.6 out of 5")`: stars filled to `value`'s share of `max`, part of a star included, kept between none and all. Screen readers read `label`, `4.6 out of 5` by default.
- BarList, SiteFavicon and CopyButton are islands taking data alone, so a static page passes them their props as it would to any element.

### RangeInput, MultiSelect, FileDrop, Menu, IconPicker

- `RangeInput(label="Hours" min={0} max={24} unit="h" value={[2, null]} onChange={hours.set})`: two number boxes for a range, each bound open when empty (`null`). `onChange([from, to])` runs once a box is committed, on blur or Enter, and only when the range changed; a reversed pair is put back in order in the boxes too. Each box is named `{label} from` and `{label} to`, or `fromLabel` and `toLabel`. `rangeFrom(low, high)` reads two strings the same way, for a server reading the posted boxes.
- `MultiSelect(label="Planets" options={planets} value={['mars']} name="planet" onChange={picked.set})`:
  - A trigger summing up what is picked (`placeholder`, `Any` by default, the one label, or "2 selected", worded by `selectedLabel(count)`) opens a popover of checkboxes with All and None, a group named by `label`. Screen readers hear the trigger as `{label}: {summary}`, a count described by the labels it stands for, and `emptyLabel` from a status region once the search hides every option.
  - Past eight options, or with `search`, the panel opens on a search box filtering the options, focused; otherwise the first checkbox takes focus. ArrowDown reaches the options, where the arrows, Home and End move between them, a tint and an accent bar marking the one the keyboard is on; Tab past the last control closes the panel, and Escape closes it with focus back on the trigger.
  - What is picked stays in the options' order, an array of the options' own value type, so a union-typed list needs no cast. `name` posts each picked value as a hidden field, so the control submits inside a plain form.
- `FileDrop(accept="image/*" multiple paste onFiles={upload})` with a `@content(zone)` block:
  - Files dropped on the zone, picked through `zone.open()` or, with `paste`, pasted anywhere on the page outside a text field, reach `onFiles(files)`: those `accept` allows, one unless `multiple`, never an empty list.
  - `zone.dragging()` reads whether files hover the zone, which also carries `data-dragging`.
  - `compact` draws it as a slim row, its content from the left, to sit inline in a form rather than as a large target.
- `Menu(label="Actions" icon="plus" items={[{ label: 'Rename', onSelect: rename }, 'separator', { label: 'Delete', icon: 'delete', danger: true, onSelect: remove }]})`:
  - An IconButton opening a `role="menu"` popover; `'separator'` draws a rule between groups, and `class` styles that button.
  - Opening focuses the first enabled entry; the arrows, Home and End move between enabled entries, an accent bar marking the one the keyboard is on, and Tab closes it.
  - An entry's `onSelect` runs once the menu has closed and focus is back on the trigger, so a dialog it opens takes focus from there.
- `IconPicker(search={findIcons} value={post.icon} name="icon" onChange={icon.set})`:
  - A search box over a grid of the icons `search(query, limit)` returns as `IconChoice`s, `{ name, icon }` with `icon` the IconProps to draw: typically an action, since a whole icon set is too large to ship, as `search={(query, limit) => findIcons({ query, limit })}`. The app's action builds them on the server with kay's `iconNames` and `iconProps` over the set's JSON, so the set never ships to the browser:

    ```ts
    import tabler from '@iconify-json/tabler/icons.json'
    import { iconNames, iconProps } from 'kay/icons'

    export const findIcons = action(t.Object({ query: t.String({ maxLength: 200 }), limit: t.Number() }), async ({ query, limit }) =>
      iconNames(tabler).filter(name => name.includes(query)).slice(0, limit).map(name => ({ name: `tabler:${name}`, icon: iconProps(tabler, name)! })))
    ```

  - The search runs 200ms after the typing pauses, from 50 icons; `Show more` asks for 50 more once a page comes back full. The last grid stays while a search is in flight, and a search a later one overtook is dropped.
  - Picking the chosen icon again, or the selection's clear button, clears it: `onChange` gets the name, or an empty string. The tooltip and label read the name without its `prefix:`.
  - `name` submits the chosen name as a hidden field, which fires a bubbling `input` event on each pick. Enter in the search box never submits the form.
  - The selection draws the chosen icon once a search found it; a `value` no search returned yet shows its name alone.
- MultiSelect and Menu draw their popover's id as Popover does, or take an `id`. RangeInput and MultiSelect take data alone, so a static page can hold them; FileDrop, Menu and IconPicker take functions, so they render inside an island.

### CommandPalette

```kay
CommandPalette(entries={[{ label: 'Moons', group: 'Pages', href: '/moons' }, { label: 'New moon', group: 'Actions', icon: 'plus', onSelect: () => creating.set(true) }]} groups={['Actions', 'Pages']} recent={recent()} onRecentChange={keepRecent})
```

- A modal search over places to go and things to do, opened and closed by Cmd on macOS and Ctrl elsewhere with `hotkey` (`k` by default) from anywhere, unless something handled the key first; `hotkey={null}` leaves opening to the app through `open`, and `onOpenChange(open)` reports each change.
- An entry has a `label`, a `group` it is listed under, an optional `icon`, and `keywords` a query matches without showing them. A `PaletteLink` has an `href`, followed in place or in a new tab with Ctrl or Cmd held, or always with `external`; a `PaletteAction` has an `onSelect`, run once the palette has closed.
- With no query, entries are listed under their groups in `groups` order, the rest after them, below the links of `recent` that still exist; following a link hands the new list to `onRecentChange(recent)`, for the app to keep.
- A query ranks the matches in one list: a label starting with it, then a label holding it, then its group or keywords, then its characters in order. The arrows walk it, wrapping, an accent bar marking the highlighted row, and Enter takes it.
- `siteSearch` searches the text of the pages too, as kay indexes them under `search: true`: a query lists the sections it finds, `{ limit }` of them, after the entries it matches, under `siteSearchLabel` (`In the pages`), each with the lines it was found in, leaving out a section an entry already links to; a followed section is not kept in `recent`, and an index that fails to load shows `siteSearchError`. It is read once, as the palette is set up.
- `label` and `placeholder` (`Search`) and `emptyLabel` (`No results`) are its words; screen readers hear how many rows a query lists from a status region, worded by `resultsLabel(count)`. It renders inside an island, since actions are functions.

### TreeView

```kay
TreeView(nodes={[{ id: 'work', label: 'Work', children: [{ id: 'specs', label: 'Specs' }] }, { id: 'inbox', label: 'Inbox', icon: 'info' }]} label="Folders" selected={folder()} onSelect={folder.set})
```

- Nested nodes, such as folders: a `TreeNode` (from the package) has an `id`, a `label`, an optional `icon`, and `children` when it is a branch, even an empty one; ids are strings, or numbers in a `TreeNode<number>[]`. `label` names the tree for screen readers.
- `selected` marks a node, drawn with the branches holding it open from the server's HTML on, and a tree whose parent passes another follows it, opening those branches; `expanded` lists the branches open to start with. `onSelect(id)` runs on a click on a row, or Enter or Space on the focused one, and the chevron opens or closes its branch alone.
- One stop in the tab order. The arrows walk the rows shown, as the ARIA tree pattern has it: Right opens a branch, then goes to its first child, Left closes it, else goes to the branch holding the row, Home and End go to the first and the last, a letter to the next row whose label starts with it. Chords stay the browser's.

### LineChart, ScatterChart, ContributionGraph

- `LineChart(label="Visits" labels={days} series={[{ name: 'Visits', values: visits }]} xLabels)`, drawn by chartist, a peer the app installs to use it: `bun add chartist`. No other component reaches it.
  - A series has a `name`, one value per label, `null` for a gap in the line, and an optional CSS `color`; without one it takes the next `--color-kui-chart-1` to `-6` token. Every line after the first is dashed in its own pattern, which the legend samples, so the series stay apart without their colours.
  - `xLabels` draws up to five x-axis labels, and spaces the points by time when every label is a date. `legend` names the series under the chart, by default once there is more than one. `formatValue` formats the y-axis, the tooltip and what screen readers hear, `toLocaleString` by default; `options` is merged over chartist's settings.
  - Hovering shows a cursor, a dot on each line and a tooltip reading every series at that point, `-` for a gap. `label` names the chart; screen readers read every value from a table only they see.
  - The plot is a `role="slider"`, one stop in the tab order on the latest point: the arrows walk the points, Home and End reach either end, and each step shows the tooltip and announces the label and every reading. Chords such as Alt with an arrow stay the browser's, and new `labels`, such as after zooming in on a span, drop the point the keyboard stood on.
  - `onRange(from, to)` lets a drag across the plot pick a span, from an island: a band follows the drag, and on release it hands over the indices of the span's first and last points, such as to zoom in on them; a press in place picks nothing. From the keyboard, Shift with the arrows, Home or End stretches the span, Enter hands it over and Escape drops it; `rangeHint` is what screen readers are told about these keys.
  - The server renders its frame, the slider, the table of values, the hint and the legend; the drawing happens once the island mounts. The table holds one row per label, so a series of thousands of points renders as many rows.
- `ScatterChart(label="Games" points={games} x={{ label: 'Hours', scale: 'log', ticks }} y={{ label: 'Score', domain: [0, 100] }} quadrant={{ x: 20, y: 80 }} corners={{ topRight: 'Long and loved' }})`:
  - A point has a `key`, a `label`, `x` and `y`, a `weight` its dot's area follows, and a `tooltip`, the label by default.
  - An axis spans its `domain`, or else the points' own extent, along a `linear` or `log` `scale`, with `ticks` of `{ value, label }` and a `label`. `quadrant` draws guides through a point, and `corners` names the four regions they split.
  - `onSelect(point)` makes each dot a button, from an island; `empty` is what it reads with no points.
- `ContributionGraph(days={days} color="var(--color-kui-accent)" today={today} months)`: a grid of weeks, each day's cell shaded towards `color` by its `intensity` from 0 to 1, with `description` as hover text before the date, which screen readers read too, or how full the day was (`50% · 2026-09-01`) without one. The grid is a group named by `label`. `days` starts on a Monday: map the dates `gridDays(weeks)` from `@kaynooo/utils/date` lists to `{ day, intensity }`, typed `ContributionDay`; `today` marks its cell, and `months` names each month over the week it starts in. It is static.

### Drag and drop: Sortable, Board, DropTargets

```kay
---
import { Sortable } from '@kaynooo/kayjs-ui/dnd'
import { attempt } from '@kaynooo/kayjs-ui'
import { signal } from 'kay'
import { reorder } from '../routes/habits.kay'

const { habits } = props<{ habits: Habit[] }>()

const rows = signal(habits)
const sortable = new Sortable({
  onReorder: (from, to) => attempt(async () => {
    const next = [...rows()]

    next.splice(to, 0, ...next.splice(from, 1))
    await reorder({ ids: next.map(habit => habit.id) })
    rows.set(next)
  }, 'Could not reorder'),
})
---
ul
  for habit of rows() key={habit.id}
    li(ref={sortable.item(habit.id)})
      button.touch-none(type="button" ref={sortable.handle(habit.id)} aria-label="Move") {habit.name}
```

- Controllers from `@kaynooo/kayjs-ui/dnd`, wired to the app's own markup through `ref`, in an island. A mouse or pen drags after a 10px move and a touch after a 250ms hold, so a swipe still scrolls, and Escape cancels. A scroll container scrolls as the pointer nears its edge. The list changes only once the callback has updated the app's data, and no other move starts until a promise it returns settles: wrap it in `attempt`, since a rejection goes unhandled.
- `Sortable({ onReorder(from, to) })`: a vertical list. `ref={sortable.item(id)}` on each entry and `ref={sortable.handle(id)}` on the part a pointer grabs, which needs `touch-action: none`. A drag slides the other items out of the way; ArrowUp and ArrowDown on a focused handle move its item one place, focus staying on it.
- `Board({ onMove({ item, from, to, index }) })`: items moving between wrapping containers and within them, for a kanban or a tier list. `ref={board.container(id)}` on each container and `ref={board.item(id, container)}` on each item, grabbed whole. A ghost follows the pointer; `board.dragging()` names the item dragged and `board.drop()` the landing `{ container, index, bar }`, the bar an insertion mark to draw `position: fixed` at `bar.left`, `bar.top` and `bar.height`. ArrowLeft and ArrowRight move a focused item within its container, ArrowUp and ArrowDown into the one before or after.
- `DropTargets({ onDrop(item, target), accepts, onLinger })`: items dropped onto targets, a move that is not a reorder, such as a note into a folder. `ref={targets.item(id)}` and `ref={targets.target(id)}`; the innermost accepting target under the pointer wins, `targets.over()` naming it and `targets.dragging()` the item. `onLinger(target)` runs once the pointer rests on a target, such as to open a folder. Pointers only: give the keyboard a menu or a dialog for the same move.
- A drag cancels the browser's own drag of a link or an image inside the item, and swallows the click its release would send.

### MarkdownEditor

- `MarkdownEditor(value={body()} onInput={body.set} onImage={upload} name="body")`: a markdown `textarea` that writes like an editor, in an island.
  - Ctrl or Cmd with B, I or K wraps the selection in bold, italics or a link; Enter continues a list, and Tab indents a list item, leaving Tab alone elsewhere and after Escape, so the keyboard can always leave the field; `keysHint` tells screen readers so, as the field's description. These go through the browser's own editing, so Ctrl+Z undoes them like typing.
  - A page pasted as HTML turns into markdown.
  - With `onImage(file)`, a pasted or dropped image is embedded behind an `![Uploading …]()` placeholder at once, swapped for `![](url)` once `onImage` resolves with its url, or removed with `uploadFailure` toasted if it throws (or a refusal of the whole call such as a limit, as `attempt` does). Writing goes on meanwhile, and a finished upload never takes focus back; the field is `aria-busy` while one is under way.
  - It shows about 12 lines and grows with its text up to 70% of the screen, where the browser sizes a field by its content (Chromium); it can be resized by hand.
  - `onInput(value)` reports the text after every change, typed or applied. A parent passing other text replaces it; passing back what it was given leaves the caret alone.

### MediaGallery, Carousel, Masonry, WhenVisible, LoadMore, ZoomPane, ImageCropper

- `MediaGallery(items={media})`: a stage, a strip of thumbnails and a lightbox.
  - An item, typed `MediaItem`, has a `key`, a `kind` (`image` or `video`), a `thumb` for the strip, a `preview` for the stage or a video's poster, a `full` the lightbox opens an image at, a video's `src`, its WebVTT `captions` and a `title`.
  - The arrows, Home and End turn it while focus is inside it, wrapping, and so do its buttons and a swipe. `index` is the item to start on, and `onIndexChange(index)` reports each turn. The strip keeps the shown thumbnail centred, and the images either side start loading.
  - A video plays in place with `preload="none"`. An `.m3u8` playlist plays through `hls.js` in browsers without native HLS, fetched only once such a video shows: an optional peer, `bun add hls.js`. An app without it still builds, and a playlist it cannot play logs that hls.js is missing.
  - An image opens full size in a lightbox, which turns the same way. `ratio` is the stage's `aspect-ratio`, `16 / 9` by default; `empty` is what it reads with no items.
- `Carousel(slides={[{ src: '/garden.jpg', alt: 'The garden' }]} autoplay={5000} ratio="4 / 3" label="Photos")`: one image at a time sliding in, for a marketing page.
  - The previous and next buttons wrap at either end, and a dot per slide jumps to it. A single slide draws no controls. `index` is the slide to start on, followed when the parent passes another, and `onIndexChange(index)` reports each turn.
  - Each slide is a `role="group"` named by `slideLabel`, where `{n}` and `{count}` stand for its number and how many there are; the hidden ones are `aria-hidden` and `inert`.
  - `autoplay` turns it every that many milliseconds, held while the pointer or the focus is on it or the tab is hidden, never for a visitor asking for reduced motion, and stopped once it leaves the page. A pause button after the controls stops it for good, until pressed again.
  - It takes data alone, so a static page holds it.
- `Masonry(items={posts} key={post => post.id} minWidth={256} gap={12})` with a `@tile(item)` block: tiles of any height in as many lanes of at least `minWidth` as fit, each dropped into the shortest lane, the order still reading left to right. The tiles are placed absolutely inside its own box, so padding goes on a wrapper, never on the Masonry; until it has measured, as on the server, they sit in a plain grid of the same lanes.
- `WhenVisible(onVisible={loadMore})`: the infinite-scroll sentinel. Render it after a list only while there is more to load; `onVisible` runs once it comes within `margin` pixels (600) of the nearest scroll box, and again whenever the list grows and leaves it in view, never again before a promise it returned settles.
- `LoadMore(list={people})` after a list, with `const people = infiniteList(firstRows, { size: 20, key: row => row.id, load: ({ offset, last }) => fetchPage(offset) })` from the package, draw `people.rows()`:
  - `size` is a full page: a shorter one ends the list. `load` resolves to the next page, `offset` counting every row fetched and `last` the last row fetched for a cursor source. One page loads at a time.
  - `key` drops a row a later page repeats; leave it out when the source cannot repeat one.
  - A `load` that throws or resolves `undefined` (an `attempt` that toasted) stops the list on an alert with a retry button, loading no other page until it is pressed.
  - It draws the WhenVisible sentinel, a `status` row while a page loads and the alert. `loadingLabel` (`Loading more…`), `failureLabel` (`Could not load more.`), `retryLabel` (`Try again`) and `margin` are its props; `people.ended()`, `failed()` and `pending()` read the state.
- `ZoomPane(label="Floor plan")` around a picture: pinch, Ctrl with the wheel, a double click, + and -, and the zoom buttons take it in, and once in the wheel alone zooms too, while fitted it scrolls the page; Ctrl with + or 0 stays the browser's zoom. A drag or the arrows move it, and 0 or the fit button fits it again. A press that does not wander stays a click, so marks standing on the picture remain clickable; `--kui-zoom-scale` lets one keep its own size with `calc(1 / var(--kui-zoom-scale))`. `tools` draws the buttons, on by default; `most` caps the zoom, 8 times fitted.
- `ImageCropper(src={photo} ratio={16 / 9} onCrop={crop.set})` with an optional `@footer(reset)` block: a crop of a fixed `ratio` over the image, centred once it loads, moved by a drag or the arrows and resized by its corners or Shift with the arrows, Alt taking bigger steps. `onCrop({ x, y, w, h })` reports it in the image's natural pixels, ready for a canvas draw; `grid` adds a rule-of-thirds overlay and `minSize` the smallest side.

## Forms

FormField frames a control with its label, hint and messages; inside an island a `group` given a message marks each input, select and textarea in it `aria-invalid` and described by the message, so `focusInvalid` reveals its tab and focuses its first field. FormDialog calls a page's action from a dialog and shows the message of each refused field on its FormField. SaveForm does the same for an editor page, with a sticky bar of unsaved changes.

```kay
--- server
import { t } from 'elysia'
import { action } from 'kay'

export const rename = action(t.Object({ id: t.String({ maxLength: 64 }), title: t.String({ minLength: 2, maxLength: 200, error: 'Two letters at least' }) }), async ({ id, title }) => posts.rename(id, title))
---
```

```kay
---
import { signal } from 'kay'
import Button from '@kaynooo/kayjs-ui/button.kay'
import FormDialog from '@kaynooo/kayjs-ui/form-dialog.kay'
import FormField from '@kaynooo/kayjs-ui/form-field.kay'
import { rename } from '../routes/posts/[id].kay'

const { post } = props<{ post: Post }>()

const editing = signal(false)
const title = signal(post.title)
---
Button(label="Rename" onClick={() => editing.set(true)})
FormDialog(open={editing()} title="Rename" action={rename} submitLabel="Rename" failure="Could not rename" onSaved={saved => title.set(saved.title)} onClose={() => editing.set(false)})
  input(type="hidden" name="id" value={post.id})
  FormField(label="Title" name="title" required)
    input.kui-field-input(name="title" value={title()})
```

- FormDialog calls `action` with `new FormData(form)`, read on the server as a plain form post and answered as a call. An action that redirects takes the browser there instead.
- When the action refuses a field, its message shows on the FormField with that `name`, and the dialog stays open.
- A refused message no FormField shows is toasted instead, a refusal of the whole form under the empty name included. A failure carrying no message toasts `failure`.
- A refusal of the handler, `ctx.fail(400, { error: 'Slug taken' })`, reaches the dialog through `refused`, which reads that data and answers a message per field (`{ slug: data.error }`), shown on the FormFields, or one message (`data.error`), toasted. Without `refused`, or when it answers undefined, `failure` is toasted: `FormDialog(... failure="Could not save" refused={data => data.error})`.
- A save hands what the action returned to `onSaved`, then closes the dialog.
- `editing<Row, Draft>()`, from the package, keeps which row one dialog adds or edits for a list: `edit(row)` opens it on a row, `create(draft)` on what a new row starts from, `close` shuts it, forgetting both, and `open()`, `row()` and `draft()` read it: `FormDialog(open={friend.open()} title={friend.row() ? 'Edit friend' : 'Add friend'} ... onClose={friend.close})`. Without `Draft`, `create()` takes nothing.
- The submit button sits in the footer, paired with the form by `id`. Without an `id`, it draws one unique on the page.
- Enter submits from a single-line field, and Ctrl+Enter from a textarea. While the call is under way, the buttons are disabled, and Escape or a click outside leaves the dialog open.
- `extra` fills the left end of the footer, for a ConfirmDelete with `trigger="button"`.

SaveForm is the form of an editor page: `SaveForm(action={rename} failure="Could not save" saved="Saved.")` around the fields, each control named as for FormDialog, draws a sticky bar with a status line, Discard and Save.

- The form is dirty while its controls differ from what they held when it was last clean, so typing a change back cleans it, and a control added or removed counts. A control set from code needs an `input` event dispatched on it.
- Save calls `action` like FormDialog, with `refused` and `failure` working the same, and does nothing while the form is clean or a save runs. A failure keeps the bar dirty, a refused field takes the focus, and edits made during the save stay unsaved. A save toasts `saved` when given, calls `onSaved(result)` and leaves the form clean.
- Discard resets the controls to their initial values, or to the saved ones once a save has run, clears the messages and calls `onDiscard`, for state the page keeps beyond the controls. The signal-driven controls (Checkbox, Toggle, ChipGroup, Segmented, Select, MultiSelect, IconPicker, TextInput, Textarea, MarkdownEditor, RangeInput) follow any `form.reset()`, a `<button type="reset">` included, and tell their `onChange` or `onInput` what they went back to.
- Leaving with unsaved changes asks as `guardLeave` does, except while a save runs. Cmd+S on macOS and Ctrl+S elsewhere save from any field, on the key that types an S whatever the layout (`shortcut('mod+s')`).
- The status line is a live region; the buttons use `aria-disabled`, so the focus stays on the one pressed as the form turns clean. `dirtyLabel`, `cleanLabel`, `savingLabel`, `saveLabel` and `discardLabel` replace the texts.

FormField also works outside a dialog, in a plain form posting to an action:

- `issue` shows a message of the page's own, such as `ctx.failed(rename)?.errors.title`.
- `hint` explains the control, under it. `action` sits at the end of the label's line. `required` marks the label with a `*` hidden from screen readers, which read the control's own `required`.
- The label holds only the label's text and the control, so the hint, the messages and the action stay out of the control's accessible name.
- Inside an island, as in a FormDialog, the control's `aria-describedby` gains the hint and, while one shows, the messages, beside the ids it had, and the control is `aria-invalid` while a message shows. A FormDialog refusing a field focuses the first one marked so. On a static page, kay marks the fields of a refused plain post `aria-invalid` itself.
- `group` makes it a `fieldset` with a `legend`, for a control made of several inputs.
- Its messages sit in an `aria-live` region, so a screen reader reads them as they appear.
- `compact` sizes it by its control rather than the row, for a filter bar of fields side by side, a Select inside as wide as its options with no class. It holds no message region then unless given a `name` or an `issue`.

A GET filter form, whose every pick lands in the URL, submits as soon as a Select changes with `submit`, no ref to the form needed:

```kay
form.flex.flex-wrap.items-end.gap-3(method="get" role="search")
  FormField(label="Period" compact)
    Select(name="period" value={filters.period} options={PERIODS} emptyOption="Last 7 days" submit)
  FormField(label="Host" compact)
    input(name="host" value={filters.host} autocomplete="off")
  Button(type="submit" label="Filter")
```

## Testing an app's use of it

A page that uses the components renders them in `testSite()` like the app's own. To test what their handlers do, `mount(file, props)` from `kay/test` renders a component of the app, once a DOM is registered, such as with `GlobalRegistrator.register()` from `@happy-dom/global-registrator`. happy-dom has no popover API, so Toaster and Popover need a shim of `showPopover`, `hidePopover`, `togglePopover` and `:popover-open` there.
